title: KV slot lease auctions and microbatch contracts for fair reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight leasing mechanism that treats KV page slots as time-bound, contestable leases. Tenants and internal microbatches bid (via a simple priority/credit contract) for short-term reservation of slots to reduce fragmentation and improve reuse without global pauses for compaction. This ticket covers the design and prototype of the lease-auction protocol, integration with microbatch contracts at the decode sender, and telemetry to measure fairness and SLO impact.
background: Paged attention workloads exhibit high slot churn caused by many short-lived requests that touch different token spans. Aggressive eviction policies reduce tail latency but increase fragmentation and cache miss cost. Existing approaches (LRU windows, deferred reclamation) either favor large tenants or require expensive background compaction. We need a runtime-level primitive that: (1) prioritizes short-term reuse when it benefits latency/cost, (2) prevents starvation from noisy tenants, and (3) composes with batching and kernel-selection heuristics.
proposal:
Implement a 'KV slot lease' primitive with the following properties:
- Lease duration: short, soft time window (e.g., 50-300ms) tied to microbatch lifecycle.
- Lease bid: a microbatch or tenant submits a bid composed of (priority score, credit token). Score is derived from SLO urgency, recent hit probability, and tenant weight.
- Auction outcome: slot owner can extend, release, or transfer a slot based on incoming bids and a simple decay-based valuation.
- Microbatch contracts: encode expected decode time and urgency in a contract attached to request; scheduler uses contracts to preemptively negotiate leases for adjacent KV pages to reduce tail re-warm cost.
- Minimal global state: auctions occur at shard-local allocator to avoid cross-shard coordination.
- Compatibility: leases operate orthogonally to existing eviction and compactors; a compactor may choose to ignore leases older than a threshold.
design_decisions:
1) Lease token vs explicit credit: we use a numeric credit token (replenished per tenant) to prevent unbounded bidding and allow cost allocation.
2) Auction algorithm: reserve-price second-price style simplified to avoid heavy computation; implement using fixed priority buckets (high/medium/low) and tie-breaker by credit.
3) Slot transfer semantics: transfers are immediate and O(1) within shard; we avoid copying KV pages on transfer by transferring ownership metadata only.
4) Duration tuning: make lease duration adaptive based on moving average of microbatch durations to reduce unnecessary hold times.
5) Safety: enforce a max-lease count per tenant to prevent monopolization and set a reclamation fast-path when memory pressure spikes.
implementation_steps:
1) Data model: add lease metadata (owner_id, expiry_ts, credit_snapshot) to slot header (backwards-compatible).
2) Allocator: extend shard-local allocator with bid queue and lightweight auction loop invoked on allocation contention.
3) Sender integration: extend microbatch contract header in decode requests to include urgency and hint for adjacent pages.
4) Scheduler: update prefill scheduler to optionally pre-negotiate leases with low-cost bids for predicted next pages.
5) Fallbacks: when auctions fail, fall back to current eviction policy.
6) Telemetry: emit per-lease events (created, extended, transferred, reclaimed), per-tenant credit usage, auction latency.
7) Tests & simulation harness: unit tests + simulator to model mixed workloads (bursting short requests vs long sessions).
8) Prototype rollout to a small canary fleet with synthetic traffic before broader rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prototype implements lease metadata and local auction loop without regressions on decode correctness.
- Simulated mixed workloads show >10% reduction in tail (95th) token latency for short requests at equal memory, and hit-rate improvement >=5% in high-churn scenarios.
- No tenant can hold >40% of slots on a shard for longer than configured max-lease-duration in steady-state tests.
- Telemetry works and includes auction metrics.
- No increase in alloc-related CPU usage >5% on canary nodes compared to baseline.
metrics:
- 95th and 99th token latency (short sessions).
- Per-shard KV hit rate and eviction rate.
- Auction success rate and average auction latency.
- Credit consumption by tenant and number of forced reclamations.
- CPU overhead on allocator path.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Unit test + local simulator (branch) — 2 weeks.
Phase 2: Canary build to 2 low-traffic shards, enable lease auctions with conservative defaults — 1 week.
Phase 3: Expand to 20% capacity, monitor metrics and customer-facing latency — 1 week.
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 60% with tuning of credit rates and lease durations — 2 weeks.
Phase 5: Full rollout if metrics stable, otherwise rollback and iterate.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator correctness and lease lifecycle.
- Integration tests where microbatch contracts are attached to decode pipeline.
- Simulator runs: generate synthetic tenants with mixed session lengths and weight distributions; validate fairness and hit-rate objectives.
- Performance bench: compare latency and CPU on canary pair.
- Chaos test: force memory pressure to validate forced reclamation safety path.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Auction adds latency on allocation hot-path. Mitigation: keep auction work O(1) with priority buckets and ensure auction loop runs only on contention.
Risk: Tenants could game credit system. Mitigation: tie credit refill to billing cadence and rate-limit refill; monitor for anomalies.
Risk: Complexity interacts badly with compactor. Mitigation: compactor honors lease age and can trigger cooperative reclamation; implement flags for compactor to bypass leases during emergency GC.
